title: Willie Smith turns down an officer's commission
summary: Willie Smith, lead alto, chose to stay with his Black colleagues.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I understand that Willie Smith was there.

Willie Smith was the lead alto player. We got him out of boot camp and brought him over there. When we got him over there and they found out who they had – they didn’t know what – he was just another dude that was in the Navy. When we got him over there, they found out he played with Jimmie Lunceford, Harry James, Charlie Spivak, [ ? ? ]. They offered him a degree, an officer’s degree, with a jacket and a cap, an ensign, offered him a degree. Willie told them, he said, “No, I’m going to stay over here with my brothers.” He was fair enough to be more caucasian than anybody up there.

If he had chosen to go, there’d have been no problem. But he was – he looked like a real caucasian. He was. You could see, but he knew there was a drop in there that made him one of us, and he said he honored it.
